title: Targeted radiation shows promise for life‑threatening kidney cancer complication
content: Diane Gentry, a 71-year-old retiree from Watauga, Texas, was diagnosed with stage 4 kidney cancer in 2015. The tumor had grown into her inferior vena cava, the body's largest vein. This potentially life-threatening complication often requires extensive surgery and carries a high risk of cancer recurrence.
summary: Diane Gentry, a 71‑year‑old retiree from Watauga, Texas, was diagnosed with stage 4 kidney cancer in 2015. The tumor had grown into her inferior vena cava, a complication that can require extensive surgery and carries a high risk of cancer recurrence.

title: Research: Indian Ocean Seasonal CO2 Absorption Changes May Strengthen Climate Buffer
content: New research published in Geophysical Research Letters indicates that seasonal patterns of carbon dioxide absorption in the Indian Ocean are changing. As the world's oceans absorb CO₂ to slow climate change, these shifts may alter how the Indian Ocean regulates Earth's climate.
summary: New research published in Geophysical Research Letters indicates that seasonal patterns of carbon dioxide absorption in the Indian Ocean are changing. These shifts may affect how the ocean helps regulate Earth's climate by slowing climate change.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists Reverse Bleached Corals in Seven Weeks, Record Speed
content: Scientists observed bleached corals on the brink of death fully recover after brief contact with healthy clones. In a laboratory setting, ghostly white corals returned to full health within seven weeks, the fastest documented recovery to date, according to a study published in Science Advances.
summary: Scientists observed bleached corals on the brink of death fully recover after brief contact with healthy clones. The recovery occurred in seven weeks, the fastest documented, according to a study published in Science Advances.

title: Penn State Grad Students Sequence First Complete Genome of Harmful Plant Pathogen
content: Graduate students in Penn State's College of Agricultural Sciences contributed to the first complete genome sequence of a harmful plant pathogen from an ornamental Prunus host. This work was completed through an active-learning activity in a plant disease diagnosis course.
summary: Graduate students in Penn State's College of Agricultural Sciences contributed to the first complete genome sequence of a harmful plant pathogen from an ornamental Prunus host. The sequencing was performed as part of an active‑learning activity in a plant disease diagnosis course.

title: Physicists prove long-suspected quantum speed limit for thermalization
content: Physicists have demonstrated a long-suspected quantum speed limit governing thermalization, the process by which an object reaches a stable, even temperature within its environment. While the time required to achieve thermal equilibrium depends on various factors, including surface area, material properties, and airflow, this newly proven limit provides a fundamental constraint on how quickly such systems can settle.
summary: Physicists have proven a long-suspected quantum speed limit for thermalization. The time it takes for an object to reach thermal equilibrium depends on factors such as surface area, material properties, and airflow.
author: Phys.org

title: Rare study shows amyloid removal linked to reduced tau buildup in Alzheimer's brain
content: A rare examination of an Alzheimer’s patient’s brain revealed a significant difference between regions cleared of amyloid plaques and neighboring areas. The cleared regions contained remarkably little harmful tau buildup associated with memory loss, while adjacent areas exhibited extensive damage. This discovery suggests that removing amyloid may provide lasting protective effects and help slow Alzheimer’s progression, particularly when treatment begins early.
summary: A rare examination of an Alzheimer's patient’s brain found that areas cleared of amyloid plaques had very little tau buildup, while adjacent regions had extensive damage. The findings suggest that amyloid removal may provide lasting protection and help slow Alzheimer's progression if treatment starts early.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists discover unusually small cancer cells with extra chromosomes are more aggressive
content: Scientists have identified that unusually small cancer cells carrying extra chromosomes can be more aggressive than larger ones. These cells grow faster, spread more readily, and resist common treatments. This discovery may help explain the danger of certain tumors and offer a new method for predicting cancer outcomes.
summary: Scientists discovered that unusually small cancer cells carrying extra chromosomes can be far more aggressive than larger ones. These cells grow faster, spread more readily, and resist common treatments, providing a new way to predict especially dangerous tumors.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Find Universal Rule Governing Black Hole Jet Eruptions
content: Scientists have discovered that black holes of vastly different sizes launch powerful jets according to the same universal rule. This breakthrough may explain why some black holes suddenly erupt years after devouring a star and could help astronomers predict when these spectacular outbursts will occur.
summary: Scientists discovered that black holes of vastly different sizes launch powerful jets according to the same universal rule. The breakthrough could explain why some black holes suddenly erupt years after devouring a star and help astronomers predict when these spectacular outbursts will happen.

title: Scientists Discover “Pac‑Man” Enzyme That Breaks Down Biodegradable Plastics in Soil
content: Scientists have identified a “Pac‑Man enzyme” that enables bacteria to digest certain plastics, offering a potential tool in the fight against plastic pollution. In laboratory tests, several biodegradable plastics fully broke down in soil within about a year, while conventional plastic remained largely unchanged.
summary: Scientists discovered a Pac‑Man enzyme that allows bacteria to digest certain plastics. The enzyme broke down several biodegradable plastics in soil within about a year, while conventional plastic remained largely unchanged.

title: Yale scientists discover cortisol's role in strengthening emotional memories
content: Yale scientists have identified how the stress hormone cortisol enables the brain to convert emotional experiences into stronger, longer-lasting memories. This discovery indicates that stress reshapes communication between brain networks responsible for emotion and memory, potentially explaining why specific moments are difficult to forget.
summary: Yale scientists found that the stress hormone cortisol helps the brain turn emotional experiences into stronger, longer-lasting memories. The study shows stress reshapes communication between brain networks involved in emotion and memory, explaining why some moments are hard to forget.

title: 24-Year Study Finds Forest Soils Increasing Methane Absorption by 3% Annually
content: Scientists have found that certain forest soils are improving their ability to absorb methane as temperatures rise and rainfall falls. A 24‑year study reported methane absorption increasing by an average of 3% per year, a result that challenges earlier predictions about how climate change will affect forest ecosystems.
summary: Scientists have discovered that some forest soils are becoming surprisingly better at removing methane from the atmosphere as temperatures rise and rainfall declines. The 24-year study found methane absorption increasing by an average of 3% annually, challenging previous predictions about climate change's effects on forests.

title: A quantum highway just one atom high could transform superconductors
content: Scientists have found that atomic steps only one atom high can direct quantum vortices in superconductors. The vortices move over 1,000 times faster in one direction than the opposite, offering precise control over quantum motion. This breakthrough could enable a new generation of ultra‑efficient superconducting electronics.
summary: Scientists discovered that atomic steps just one atom high can guide quantum vortices through superconductors, making them move more than 1,000 times more easily in one direction than another. This remarkable control over quantum motion could lead to a new generation of ultra-efficient superconducting electronics.
author: Science Daily

title: James Webb finds atmospheric bulge on gas giant WASP-17b
content:
Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have discovered that the atmosphere of the distant gas giant WASP-17b is surprisingly lopsided. The planet, located 1,300 light‑years away, is a scorching gas giant whose powerful winds redistribute heat across its atmosphere.

A new mapping technique revealed that these winds cause one side of the planet’s atmosphere to bulge outward. The observation confirms predictions about how extreme temperatures and winds shape alien worlds.
summary: Scientists using the James Webb Space Telescope found that the atmosphere of the gas giant WASP-17b is lopsided, with a bulge on one side. A new mapping technique showed that powerful winds redistribute heat, creating the outward bulge.
author: Science Daily

title: The Guardian view on plague in Russia: what is most worrying is the lack of information | Editorial
content:
In the three weeks since a health worker at a Siberian plague research unit died of a mysterious respiratory illness, Russian officials have been tight‑lipped about the circumstances and whether additional cases have emerged. This lack of information has prompted the World Health Organization and the international community to express concern, citing the small but real risk of a plague outbreak.

The Guardian editorial notes that, if an outbreak were confirmed, swift medical intervention would make plague treatable. However, the uncertainty surrounding the incident has highlighted a growing problem: the erosion of international coordination that is essential for pandemic prevention. The editorial warns that this trend could undermine future efforts to protect global health.
summary: In the three weeks since a health worker’s death in Siberia, officials have stonewalled the WHO – setting a worrying precedent for future pandemics Is there a plague outbreak in Russia? If the answer were a clear yes, there shouldn’t be much reason to worry.
author: Guardian Science

title: Rep. Torres Introduces Power To The Players Act to Ensure Game Ownership
content:
Rep. Ritchie Torres of New York’s 15th congressional district in the Bronx introduced the Power To The Players Act this week. The bill would direct the Federal Trade Commission to establish regulations that guarantee consumers ownership of a game when they pay for it, rather than a licensing agreement.

Torres points to the growing problem of games that require a server connection. When a company shuts down those servers, the games often become unplayable. He cites NBA 2K25 as a recent example, noting that 2K will be delisting the game from storefronts at the end of the month and shutting down its servers on an upcoming date.
summary: Rep. Ritchie Torres of New York's 15th congressional district in the Bronx introduced the Power To The Players Act this week.

title: Anthropic Grants External Evaluators Employee-Like Access to Claude Systems
content:
Anthropic has granted external evaluators “employee‑like access” to assess the risks of its models, following a commitment to increase safeguards over concerns the technology could run catastrophically out of control.

METR, a nonprofit that has worked with leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office with access to its hardware and internal systems.

A greater role for third‑party evaluators is among the main concrete steps the labs have proposed in response to rising concern about the dangers more capable AI systems could pose to the economy, cyber security and humanity at large.
summary: Anthropic has granted external evaluators employee-like access to assess the risks of its models. METR, a nonprofit, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office with access to its hardware and internal systems.

content: On Sunday 18 October, residents in France found streets in Paris, Lyon and Marseille littered with broken glass, burnt bicycles and other debris. The damage was a result of demonstrations that left extensive destruction across the three cities.
summary: Streets in Paris, Lyon and Marseille were littered with broken glass, burnt bicycles and debris on Sunday 18 October. The damage was caused by demonstrations that left extensive damage across the three cities.

content: US President Donald Trump endorsed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday ahead of Israel's October 27 elections. The impact of the endorsement remains unclear, as many Israelis have expressed disappointment with Trump over the outcome of the Iran war and his ceasefire proposal.

content: Fresh clashes erupted in Paris on Sunday, following a day of significant unrest across France. Protests against high prices resulted in one demonstrator’s death, thousands of arrests, and widespread looting and damage to shops nationwide.
summary: Fresh clashes broke out in Paris on Sunday, a day after France experienced one of its worst bouts of unrest in years. Protests over high prices left one demonstrator dead, thousands arrested, and shops across the country looted or damaged.

content: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that France was “burning” and that the country was “shattered” by immigration, blaming the influx of migrants for the unrest during recent protests. title: Six-year-old and 35-year-old killed when truck drives through Wichita soccer game
content:
Two people were killed on Saturday when a truck drove through a youth soccer game in north-east Wichita, Kansas. Authorities identified the victims as a six-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man. Additionally, eleven other individuals, ranging in age from five to 68, were injured in the incident. Wichita police took a 34-year-old truck driver from Garden City into custody in connection with the case.

The possible motivations for the attack remained unclear early Sunday, although the incident continued to capture widespread attention across the United States.
summary: A 34‑year‑old truck driver from Garden City was taken into custody after a truck drove through a youth soccer game in north‑east Wichita, killing a six‑year‑old boy and a 35‑year‑old man. Eleven other people aged five to 68 were injured, and the possible motivations remain unclear.

title: Microsoft pulls out of Nscale AI datacentre project in Essex over power supply concerns
content:
Microsoft has withdrawn from an AI datacentre project in Loughton, Essex, citing concerns about power supplies. The company’s exit marks a setback for the development, which had been promoted by UK ministers as the country’s largest AI datacentre.

The project, led by British firm Nscale, was announced in 2025 and was scheduled to open next year. With Microsoft no longer an anchor tenant, the development faces a fresh challenge as it moves forward.
summary: Microsoft has pulled out of the Nscale AI datacentre project in Essex because of power supply concerns. The project, announced in 2025, was planned to open next year at Loughton and was heralded by ministers as the UK's largest AI datacentre.

title: Manchester City owner’s £55m housing loan under scrutiny during Burnham's mayoralty
content:
A scrutiny committee will investigate a £55 million loan that went to Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi owner. The review focuses on a fund for housing projects that was set up while Andy Burnham served as the city’s mayor.

The investigation follows weeks of scrutiny of the prime minister’s links to Manchester City’s owners after the club was found guilty of boosting its income by £900 million in a nine‑year breach of financial rules.

title: Hull mayor Luke Campbell investigated for allegedly sharing naked images with staff
content:
Police in Humberside are investigating Luke Campbell, the Reform UK mayor of Hull and East Yorkshire, over allegations that he showed “naked and sexualised” images of himself to a female member of staff. Campbell, a former Olympic boxing champion, was questioned under caution by Humberside police earlier this month.

A female colleague has said she was forced out of her position shortly after the incident. The investigation continues as authorities examine the claims.
summary: A Reform UK mayor and former Olympic boxing champion Luke Campbell is under police investigation for allegedly showing naked and sexualised images of himself to a female staff member. A female colleague says she was forced out shortly after the incident, and Campbell was questioned under caution by Humberside police earlier this month.

title: Cockroach Janata leaders Ranka, Das jailed five days for Jantar Mantar protest breach
content:
Two leaders of the youth‑led Cockroach Janata Party, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, have been ordered to serve five days in Delhi’s Tihar prison. A court ruled that the pair violated a ban on protests at Jantar Mantar, a historic site in central Delhi that authorities had closed, after they jumped police barricades, raised slogans and waved the Indian flag.

The sentencing follows the court’s finding that Ranka and Das entered the restricted area despite the prohibition, prompting the five‑day jail term for each.
summary: A court ordered Cockroach Janata party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das to spend five days in Delhi’s Tihar prison. They were jailed for jumping police barricades, holding up slogans and waving the Indian flag at the banned protest site Jantar Mantar.

title: US ambassador Huckabee calls West Bank settler attack on American photojournalist terror
content:
U.S. ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemned a recent West Bank incident in which Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, 63, was severely beaten. Huckabee described the settler assault as a “despicable act of terror” and urged that those responsible be arrested and prosecuted.

Levine, an award‑winning journalist residing in Israel, was attacked last Friday by masked Israeli settlers who used clubs and other weapons while confronting Palestinians harvesting olives in occupied West Bank towns. The assault left her badly injured, requiring surgery, and she is now recovering in an Israeli hospital.
summary: Mike Huckabee calls for arrest and prosecution of those responsible as Heidi Levine, 63, recovers in hospital in Israel The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced the settler attack that left the Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine badly beaten and needing surgery as a “despicable act of terror” and called for the arrest and prosecution of those responsible. Levine, an award-winning journalist who lives in Israel, was set upon last Friday by masked Israeli settlers who used clubs and other weapons to attack Palestinian people attempting to harvest their olives in occupied West Bank towns.

content:
Watford manager Alessio Dionisi has issued an apology to Elton John, a development highlighted in the latest edition of Football Daily. The Italian coach’s statements also confirmed that the club’s owners have not yet dismissed him, despite reports suggesting the management group is prone to quick firings. title: Barcelona beat Real Betis 5-2 to reach nine straight La Liga wins
content:
Barcelona maintained their perfect La Liga record by defeating Real Betis 5-2 in Seville, securing their ninth consecutive win and extending their league goal tally to 39. Lamine Yamal opened the scoring with a dazzling strike, followed by goals from Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric García, and substitute Dani Olmo. Real Betis, who played much of the second half with ten men after Facundo Bernal was sent off for head-butting Yamal, managed replies through Valentín Gómez and Ez Abde.

In other European football action, Luis Díaz scored a hat-trick to help Bayern Munich thump RB Leipzig 6-1.
summary: Barcelona defeated Real Betis 5-2 on Saturday, extending their winning streak to nine games in La Liga. Lamine Yamal opened the scoring, and Facundo Bernal was sent off for head-butting Yamal during the match.

title: Haaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat Ipswich
content:
Enzo Maresca has become the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games, guiding Manchester City to a victory over Ipswich Town. This achievement stands out amidst the ongoing controversy following the club’s guilty verdict for breaching financial rules, an event that has drawn significant criticism from fans and the public. Despite the surrounding noise, the focus shifted to the pitch as City secured a crucial home win, moving six points clear in the standings.

The match featured a resilient performance from Ipswich Town, who put up a fight against the league leaders. Phil Foden opened the scoring for Manchester City, instigating the triumph with a notable celebration. Erling Haaland then secured the points for the hosts, ensuring the victory despite late pressure from Ipswich. The visitors created several scares during the game, with Daizen Maeda and Zian Flemming threatening the City defense before the final whistle.
summary: There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats”, but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games.

title: Manzambi heads winner as Aston Villa beat Newcastle
content:
Aston Villa secured a win over Newcastle, with Johan Manzambi heading the winner. The 21‑year‑old Switzerland attacking midfielder, who had been linked with a summer move from Freiburg to Newcastle, instead delighted Villa fans and demonstrated why the club paid a record £50 million plus fee.  

The victory came at a time when Premier League CEO Richard Masters sat in the directors’ box, watching the two clubs most affected by the spending rules he has overseen. For Newcastle’s manager, Matthias Jaissle, the irony was stark: Manzambi’s goal sealed a dismal week for the Tynesiders.
summary: Johan Manzambi scored the winning goal for Aston Villa in their match against Newcastle. The 21-year-old Swiss midfielder had recently transferred from Freiburg to Villa for a record fee.

title: Kartal battles past Ostapenko in Wuhan to secure spot in first WTA 1000 final
content:
Sonay Kartal defeated former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko in straight sets on Saturday to advance to the final of the Wuhan Open, marking the biggest final of her career. The 24‑year‑old fought back from a deficit in both sets, winning 7‑6 (9), 7‑6 (5) after saving six set points.

Kartal’s victory comes in her second tour‑level tournament after a six‑month injury layoff. She entered the week ranked world No 170 due to recent inactivity, making her the lowest‑ranked player to reach a WTA 1000 final since the format began in 2009.

The win guarantees Kartal a jump into the world’s top 50 next week, overtaking Katie Boulter and becoming the new British No 1.
summary: The 24-year-old becomes new British No 1 Biggest final of career after six months out with injury Sonay Kartal’s dream comeback continues as the Briton beat Jelena Ostapenko in straight sets on Saturday to advance to the biggest final of her career at the Wuhan Open. Kartal was behind in both sets and fought off six set points to claim a 7-6 (9), 7-6 (5) win over the former French Open champion in her second tour-level tournament back after injury.

content:

content: Sen. title: Rising CPI to 3.7% in September adds pressure on GOP ahead of midterms
content: Recent economic data present a bleak outlook as early‑voting for the midterms proceeds, dealing another setback to Republicans. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Wednesday that annual inflation measured by the consumer price index rose from 3.4 % in August to 3.7 % in September. A day later the BLS released wholesale‑price information, adding further pressure on GOP prospects.
summary: Recent data paints a bleak picture of the economy, lending Republicans another blow as midterm early-voting is underway. Annual inflation, as measured by the consumer price index (CPI), rose from 3.4 percent in August to 3.7 percent in September, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported Wednesday.
author: The Hill

title: Federico Veronesi wins Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026; exhibit at NHM London
content:
The Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 competition has announced its winners, presenting a selection of images that span subjects from underwater scenes to urban wildlife, photojournalism and mammal behaviour. The overall prize went to Italy’s Federico Veronesi for his striking photograph of an elephant carrying a dead calf.

All winning photographs will be displayed at London’s Natural History Museum, with the exhibition opening on 16 October 2026 and running through July 2027.
summary: The overall winner of the Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 is Federico Veronesi of Italy for his image of an elephant carrying a dead calf. The winning photographs will be displayed at the Natural History Museum in London from 16 October 2026 until July 2027.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Scottish athlete Archie Goodburn meets Andy Burnham after TV brain cancer appeal
content: Scottish athlete Archie Goodburn, diagnosed two years ago with three inoperable brain tumours, delivered an emotional TV plea urging more investment in brain‑cancer research. After the appeal, he met with Andy Burnham, who responded to the call for increased funding.
summary: Scottish athlete Archie Goodburn, diagnosed with three inoperable brain tumours two years ago, made an emotional TV plea for more investment into brain cancer research. He later met Andy Burnham following the appeal.
author: BBC Health

title: Mantis shrimp red-sensitive pigments act as reversible light switches
content: Researchers from the University of Liège and Humboldt University in Berlin have, for the first time, examined mantis shrimp visual pigments individually. Their analysis identified several red‑sensitive pigments—rare among animals—in a system that contains roughly 30 pigments compared with the three found in humans. The results, detailed in Science Advances, suggest these pigments function as reversible light switches and could be leveraged for optogenetic applications.
summary: Researchers from ULiège and Humboldt University in Berlin analyzed mantis shrimp visual pigments individually and found that some red‑sensitive pigments act as reversible light switches. The study, published in Science Advances, notes that these pigments detect red light rarely perceived by other animals and could be useful for optogenetics.
author: Phys.org

title: FAST telescope finds hydrogen cloud with 500,000 solar masses, possible dark galaxy
content:
Astronomers using China’s FAST radio telescope have discovered a compact cloud of hydrogen with no visible stars or galaxy around it.  

The object, containing nearly 500,000 times the sun’s mass in neutral hydrogen, is described as one of the strongest isolated “dark galaxy” candidates. The discovery was detailed in a paper posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 24.
summary: Astronomers using China's FAST radio telescope discovered a compact cloud of hydrogen with no visible stars or galaxy around it. The cloud, containing nearly 500,000 times the sun's mass in neutral hydrogen, is a strong candidate for an isolated dark galaxy, and the discovery paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 24.
author: Phys.org

title: James Webb finds three-state orderly weather on turbulent world 20 ly away
content:
NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has revealed that a turbulent world 20 light‑years away exhibits an orderly weather system.  

The system cycles through three recurring atmospheric states driven by temperature shifts and cloud movements, a breakthrough that provides scientists a new tool to study weather patterns on distant planets and the atmospheric conditions that shape them.
summary: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope revealed that a turbulent world 20 light‑years away has a surprisingly orderly weather system. The system shows three recurring atmospheric states driven by temperature changes and shifting clouds, giving scientists a new tool for studying distant worlds’ weather patterns.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists link dysfunctional brain cells to abnormal myelin and cognitive decline
content:
Scientists have identified that certain protective brain cells may actually drive age‑related cognitive decline. When these cells malfunction, they generate excess myelin, which interferes with nerve fiber integrity.  

The disruption is linked to worsening memory and thinking abilities in older individuals.
summary: Scientists have uncovered a cause of age‑related cognitive decline involving brain cells previously thought to be entirely beneficial. When these cells become dysfunctional they can produce abnormal amounts of myelin, disrupting nerve fibers and potentially contributing to worsening memory and thinking skills.
author: Science Daily

title: Stanford scientists unveil microscope that images living cells in real time without labels
content:
Stanford scientists have developed a revolutionary microscope that reveals the hidden inner workings of living cells in real time, without the fluorescent labels that can interfere with observations.  

The breakthrough could provide new insights into cancer, infectious diseases and how drugs interact with cells.
summary: Stanford scientists have developed a revolutionary microscope that reveals the hidden inner workings of living cells in real time without fluorescent labels. The breakthrough could provide new insights into cancer, infectious diseases, and how drugs interact with cells.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists discover European nightjar trades speed for agility, generates upward thrust
content:
Scientists have uncovered an unexpected trade‑off in the wings of the European nightjar, a bird that migrates thousands of kilometres.  

The species sacrifices high‑speed flight efficiency to hunt insects with remarkable agility and generates thrust on the upward wingbeat, a technique that could inspire new flying technologies.
summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected trade‑off in the wings of the European nightjar, which migrates thousands of kilometers but sacrifices high‑speed flight efficiency to hunt insects with remarkable agility. The bird also generates thrust on the upward wingbeat, a technique that could inspire new flying technologies.
author: Science Daily

title: SpaceX delivers strange cargo including brain models and retinal tech to ISS
content:
SpaceX delivered a notably unconventional payload to the International Space Station, according to the latest shipment report.  

The cargo includes tiny brain models, three‑dimensional heart tissue and equipment for manufacturing artificial retinas in microgravity, experiments that scientists say could lead to new treatments for severe brain disorders, restore vision and enable testing of future medicines.  

Also aboard are materials intended to produce unusual glass in near weightlessness and the station’s final upgraded solar arrays.
summary: SpaceX delivered a cargo shipment to the International Space Station that includes tiny brain models, 3D heart tissue, and technology for making artificial retinas in space. The shipment also contains materials for creating unusual glass in near weightlessness and the station’s final upgraded solar arrays.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope delivers image quality about 30% better than expected
content: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has outperformed its design specifications after engineers made minute adjustments to its optics. By shifting a mirror by an amount equivalent to one‑sixteenth the width of a human hair, the team aligned the telescope’s instruments with near‑perfect precision. The correction boosted the Wide Field Instrument’s image quality to nearly 30 % better than originally predicted, enhancing the telescope’s capability for exceptionally sharp cosmic surveys.
summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope exceeded expectations after engineers moved a mirror by one‑sixteenth the width of a human hair to improve alignment. Roman’s Wide Field Instrument now achieves image quality nearly 30% better than predicted, enabling sharper cosmic surveys.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA discovers dozens of hidden fires beneath Amazon rainforest
content:
NASA researchers have uncovered dozens of previously undetected fires burning beneath the Amazon rainforest, suggesting the damage may be more extensive than satellite records indicate.

Scientists say El Niño is driving a dangerous cascade of wildfires across the tropics, with the Amazon now seeing widespread burning and warnings that the worst could still be ahead.
summary: El Niño is fueling a dangerous cascade of wildfires across the tropics, with the Amazon rainforest now experiencing widespread burning. NASA researchers are uncovering dozens of previously undetected fires, suggesting the destruction could be more extensive than satellite records show.
author: Science Daily

title: SpaceX Falcon 9 launch creates jellyfish-shaped glow over eastern US
content: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launched early morning, creating a jellyfish‑shaped glow across the eastern United States as sunlight illuminated its exhaust. The NASA mission delivered equipment and scientific experiments to the International Space Station, including research aimed at advancing treatments for blindness, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and other diseases.
summary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launched early in the morning, producing a jellyfish-shaped glow across the eastern United States as sunlight illuminated its exhaust. The mission delivered equipment and scientific experiments to the International Space Station, including research aimed at advancing treatments for blindness, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and other diseases.
author: Science Daily

title: Pete Hegseth’s livestream execution plan condemned, but experts say many will watch
content:
US defence secretary Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan has drawn condemnation from human rights groups and politicians across the spectrum.  

Coltan Scrivner, an author and psychologist at Arizona State University, says that despite the backlash, large numbers are likely to watch, explaining the attraction to dark and disturbing content.  

Madeleine Finlay tells Ian Sample that consuming such material can harm observers’ mental health.
summary: US defence secretary Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan has incurred condemnation from human rights groups and politicians on all sides. But according to Coltan Scrivner, an author and psychologist at Arizona State University and expert on morbid curiosity, people are still likely to watch in large numbers.
author: Guardian Science

title: Creator builds Zelda timeline ahead of Ocarina of Time remake release
content:
A Hacker News user posted a “Show HN” entry titled “The Zelda timeline to catch up before the Ocarina of Time remake,” unveiling a personal visual timeline created in anticipation of the upcoming remake, which is slated to arrive in 17 days. The creator said the project was motivated by a childhood recollection of playing the game and a desire to refresh the story using Nintendo’s official timeline as the reference point, citing Hyrule Historia and the company’s chronicle page.

The timeline visualizes the narrative split at the conclusion of Ocarina of Time, branching into three separate eras depending on whether Link succeeds or fails, with each era depicted as an individual thread on a cloth‑like layout. Those threads later reconverge in the era of Breath of the Wild. The author noted assistance from the AI tool Claude and explained that the project was undertaken despite a busy schedule balancing a day job and other responsibilities.

The post has drawn modest community engagement, earning 29 points and six comments on the Hacker News discussion thread.
summary: A creator made a visual Zelda timeline to catch up before the Ocarina of Time remake, which arrives in 17 days. The timeline follows Nintendo’s official chronology, showing the post‑Ocarina branches into three eras that later converge in Breath of the Wild.
author: Hacker News

title: Lenovo Legion Go S handheld with SteamOS discounted to $999.99 at Best Buy
content:
Lenovo’s Legion Go S handheld, now running SteamOS, is being sold at a discounted price of $999.99 at Best Buy, down from its listed $1,579.99. The device pairs the Ryzen Z1 Extreme processor with 32 GB of RAM and a 1 TB solid‑state drive, and it features an eight‑inch IPS panel that delivers 1080p resolution at up to 120 Hz—specifications that surpass the $789 Steam Deck OLED’s 800p screen and 90 Hz refresh rate.

The Go S also includes two‑stage triggers and a design aimed at comfort, positioning it as a solid alternative to the Deck. While it offers more power than the Steam Deck, it trails the $1,299.99 Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20, which uses a Ryzen Z2 Extreme chip and an OLED display.

The model originally launched with Windows 11 and a Ryzen Z2 Go processor, but the discounted configuration swaps in the faster Z1 Extreme and SteamOS for a better handheld experience. For further performance details, readers can refer to Sean Hollister’s review and benchmarks of the Go S configurations.
summary: The Legion Go S with SteamOS is a pretty solid alternative to the $789 Steam Deck OLED. It runs identical software, but ships in a design with two-stage triggers, a bigger eight-inch IPS screen (1080p and up to 120Hz versus 800p and 90Hz in the Deck OLED), and it’s got double the RAM and storage (32GB and 1TB, respectively), not to mention a slightly faster processor in the Ryzen Z1 Extreme.
author: The Verge

title: Looters raid and vandalise shops across France during massive protests
content: Looters on Saturday took advantage of massive protests across France, raiding and vandalising a range of shops and businesses, from bakeries and supermarkets to tech stores. The attacks unfolded while hundreds of thousands of people were on the streets protesting higher living costs and other grievances.
summary: Looters on Saturday raided and vandalised a range of shops and businesses across France, from bakeries and supermarkets to tech stores. The attacks took place while hundreds of thousands of people were on the streets protesting higher living costs and other grievances.
author: France 24

title: Atlanta ‘No Kings’ rally urges vote, denounces Trump ahead of midterms
content: “No Kings, Vote Now” was the theme of a rally in Atlanta on Saturday, part of a series of events across the US. Demonstrators denounced President Donald Trump’s policies, and organizers said the gathering aimed to boost turnout for the November 3 midterm elections and protect American democracy.
summary: The “No Kings, Vote Now” rally was held in Atlanta on Saturday as part of a series of events across the United States. Demonstrators criticized President Donald Trump’s policies and organizers said the rally aimed to boost turnout for the November 3 midterm elections and protect American democracy.
author: France 24

title: Rubio says Trump’s 60‑day pause on Russia sanctions to be analyzed globally
content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that President Donald Trump will pause waiving sanctions and tariffs on Russia for 60 days and will analyze the global impact of the sanctions during that pause.  

The decision has drawn bipartisan criticism and sparked concerns in Ukraine that Washington may further ease restrictions on Moscow.
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sanctions and tariffs on Russia will last 60 days. He noted the move has drawn bipartisan criticism and raised concerns in Ukraine that Washington could further ease restrictions on Moscow.
author: France 24

title: Macron to address nation at 8 pm after protests with over 1,800 arrests
content:
French President Emmanuel Macron will address the nation at 8 p.m. this evening after Saturday’s demonstrations that resulted in more than 1,800 arrests alongside peaceful marches.  

U.S. President Donald Trump reacted on his Truth Social platform, declaring “France is burning,” as the liveblog continues to track developments.
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron will address the nation at 8 pm following Saturday's demonstrations that led to more than 1,800 arrests and included peaceful marches. US President Donald Trump said “France is burning” on his Truth Social platform.
author: France 24

title: India releases Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke from police custody
content:
Indian police released Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke from detention on Saturday after he had been held ahead of a rally demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner.  

Two other CJP leaders remain in custody, having been arrested while demonstrating at a protest site that police had declared off‑limits.
summary: Indian police released Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke from detention on Saturday. Two other CJP leaders remain in custody after being arrested while demonstrating at a police‑restricted protest site.
author: France 24

title: India’s youth‑led Cockroach movement faces crackdown, leaders jailed, protest site closed
content:
A fresh wave of demonstrations by India’s youth‑led Cockroach movement has encountered a harsh crackdown from Narendra Modi’s government, which also ordered the closure of a historic protest site in Delhi.  

Two movement leaders were detained for five days after authorities said they breached suppression measures. The protests, originally sparked by frustration over education and unemployment, have shifted to demand voting‑rights protections. Modi’s government rejects accusations that it aims to disenfranchise millions of voters, while the United Nations and Amnesty International have condemned the treatment of demonstrators, warning that India may be sliding toward autocracy. Lucy Hough interviews South Asia correspondent Hannah Ellis‑Petersen on the issue.
summary: A fresh wave of protests by India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has been met with a brutal crackdown by Narendra Modi’s government and the closure of a historic protest site in Delhi. Two of the movement’s leaders have been imprisoned for five days for violating suppression measures.
author: Guardian World

title: Roof collapse at al-Khair school in Peshawar kills at least 34 children and a teacher
content:
A roof collapse at the privately run al‑Khair school in Peshawar killed at least 34 schoolchildren and a female teacher during morning classes.

Rescue workers spent hours pulling children from the rubble, while three pupils remain in critical condition. Panicked parents and relatives thronged the site searching for loved ones.
summary: At least 34 schoolchildren and a female teacher died when the roof of the privately run al‑Khair school collapsed during morning classes in the northern Pakistani city of Peshawar. Three additional pupils are in critical condition as rescue workers continue searching for survivors.
author: Guardian World

title: Cockroach Janta party leader Abhijeet Dipke arrested in Delhi ahead of protest
content: The leader of the Cockroach Janta Party youth movement, Abhijeet Dipke, was detained by police on Friday and subsequently formally arrested as authorities intensified a crackdown on fresh anti‑government protests in Delhi. Dipke had called for a Friday‑evening demonstration in central Delhi, urging supporters to gather and hold up the Indian flag. Police detained him shortly before the planned rally, citing the broader effort to suppress the newly organized protests.
summary: Abhijeet Dipke, leader of the Cockroach Janta party youth movement, was detained by police on Friday in Delhi. He was later formally arrested as authorities cracked down on fresh anti‑government protests before a planned evening demonstration he had called.
author: Guardian World

title: Reviewers Praise Guardian’s NAZA Documentary on Gaza Civilian Mass Killing
content:
Critics worldwide have praised the award‑winning documentary NAZA, describing it as “brilliant and harrowing” and “impossible to ignore.” The film, produced by the Guardian, features interviews with military insiders about the mass killing of civilians in Gaza.

NAZA opened in UK cinemas this week and is slated for theatrical release in more than 50 countries. In addition to its global cinema rollout, the documentary will be available for free on the Guardian’s website from late November.
summary: Film interviewing military insiders about mass killing of civilians in Gaza wins widespread praise around the world Critics around the world have hailed the award-winning documentary NAZA as a “brilliant and harrowing” film that is “impossible to ignore”. NAZA, which is produced by the Guardian and details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, was released in UK cinemas this week and will be shown in more than 50 countries.
author: Guardian World

title: Israeli settlers attack olive harvesters and Washington Post photographer in West Bank
content:
Israeli settlers launched coordinated attacks on Palestinians harvesting olives in the occupied West Bank on Friday, targeting farmers and Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine as part of a yearly effort to disrupt the olive harvest.  

Masked settlers wielding clubs, rocks and other weapons hurled projectiles at the harvesters, beat the journalist and set fire to cars and trees. Palestinian authorities said the assaults occurred in eight villages and left at least 20 people injured.
summary: Masked Israeli settlers wielding clubs, rocks and other weapons attacked Palestinians harvesting olives in West Bank towns, burning cars and trees and beating Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine. Palestinian authorities said the coordinated attacks occurred in eight villages and injured at least 20 people.
author: Guardian World

title: Gaza war separates Wijdan Abu Matar from injured husband after 17 Oct strike
content:
Wijdan Abu Matar, 43, was compelled to leave Gaza in November 2023 with her eight children for medical treatment, leaving her injured husband, Hatem, behind. The family resided in the Nuseirat refugee camp when the conflict began following the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack on Israel. On 17 October, an Israeli strike targeted the al-Muhandseen tower near their home, injuring Wijdan and every other member of the family.

This incident exemplifies how the war has scattered families and prevented couples from reuniting or marrying. Wijdan’s separation from her husband highlights the broader struggle of individuals unable to carry the burden of displacement and injury alone amidst the ongoing crisis.
summary: Families have been scattered, fathers separated from their children, and couples unable to reunite and marry Wijdan Abu Matar, 43, was forced to leave Gaza in November 2023 with her eight children for medical treatment, while her injured husband, Hatem, remained behind. Wijdan and her family were living in the Nuseirat refugee camp when the Gaza war began with the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack on Israel.
author: Guardian World

title: UAE to resume payments to Yemeni forces as Saudi Arabia provides air cover
content:
The United Arab Emirates has agreed to re‑enter the Yemen conflict by resuming payments to certain government forces fighting the Iran‑aligned Houthi fighters in the south, according to Yemeni sources. In exchange, Saudi Arabia will provide air cover for the anti‑Houthi forces.

The arrangement marks the first concrete sign that the long‑standing rift between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over Yemen’s future is beginning to heal, driven by recent Houthi advances that have alarmed Gulf state rulers. Both Gulf nations are coordinating their support as the Houthi gains intensify, signaling a renewed joint effort to bolster the Yemeni government side against the rebel group.
summary: The United Arab Emirates has agreed to re‑enter the Yemen conflict by resuming payments to some government forces fighting Iran‑aligned Houthis in the south. Saudi Arabia will provide air cover for those anti‑Houthi forces, marking a new cooperation between the two Gulf states.
author: Guardian World

title: French government in crisis talks after violent unrest burns buildings, 2000 arrested
content:
The French government entered crisis talks on Sunday after a day of unrest described as one of the most violent in years, during which public buildings were set ablaze, hundreds of shops were destroyed and looted, and more than 2,000 people were arrested across the country.  

Ministers, officials and police are under pressure as politicians from both the left and right have called for the resignation of interior minister Laurent Nuñez, saying the administration was caught by surprise by the scale of the violence that saw state buildings stormed and torched, bus stops smashed, roads barricaded and shops broken into and destroyed.
summary: Ministers, officials and police under pressure over response to days of violent unrest in cities across France The French government was in crisis talks on Sunday after one of the most violent days of unrest in years left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted, and more than 2000 people arrested in cities across the country. Politicians on the left and right called for the resignation of the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, after the government appeared to have been caught by surprise by the scale of violence as state buildings were stormed and torched, bus stops smashed, roads barricaded and shops broken into and destroyed.
author: Guardian World

title: The X-Files' is officially returning as Hulu picks up Ryan Coogler's 'reimagining' of the sci-fi icon
content:
Disney and Hulu announced today that they have ordered a full‑season “The X‑Files” series, described as a “reimagining” of the classic sci‑fi franchise. The new project is being led by Ryan Coogler, the writer‑director behind “Creed,” “Black Panther” and “Sinners,” who wrote, directed and executive‑produced the pilot. Coogler said he has long loved the original series and aimed to honor its legacy while forging a new path.

The show will star Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel as two highly decorated but very different FBI agents who are assigned to a long‑shuttered division that investigates unexplained phenomena. Supporting cast members include Amy Madigan, Ben Foster, Devery Jacobs, Lochlyn Munro, Tantoo Cardinal, Joel D. Montgrand, Sofia Grace Clifton and Steve Buscemi.

Original creator Chris Carter is attached as an executive producer, though both Coogler and Hulu have been vague about how the series will fit into the existing continuity, noting only that it is a reimagining rather than a reboot. No release date has been set, but the series will launch exclusively on Hulu in the United States and Disney+ in the United Kingdom.
summary: The truth is once again out there, as Disney & Hulu confirmed today that they have picked up a new "The X-Files" show for a full season. Described as a "reimagining" of the classic series, the project comes from Ryan Coogler, the acclaimed writer and director of "Creed", "Black Panther", and "Sinners", and will star Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel.
author: Space.com

title: ‘Testosterone to burn’: Kagiso Rabada plays down 2018 clash with Australia’s Steve Smith
content:
Kagiso Rabada says “There’s no hate,” as he prepares to return to St George’s Park, downplaying the heated 2018 clash with Australia’s Steve Smith that unfolded in Gqeberha six years ago. The South African fast‑bowler insists there is no lingering bad blood with the visitors ahead of the second Test.

Rabada has been declared fit after a hamstring tear and will face Australia in his first match since May. His comeback comes at a crucial stage, with the hosts fighting to stay alive after their 214‑run pumping in Durban last week.
summary: ‘There’s no hate,’ says bowler ahead of return to St George’s Park Pair clashed in Gqeberha during heated series six years ago Kagiso Rabada insists there is no lingering bad blood with Australia as the South Africa speedster prepares to return to the site of his controversial clash with Steve Smith. Rabada has been declared fit to come back from his hamstring tear and face Australia in the second Test at St George’s Park, in his first match since May.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts placed on IR after calf blood clot diagnosis
content:
Quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after the Philadelphia Eagles confirmed he had a blood clot in his calf.  

Hurts was first ruled out on Thursday for the Eagles’ upcoming game against Carolina after the team said he had been injured when he took a cleat to his calf during their game against the Los Angeles Rams on October 4.  

The Eagles said the blood clot requires Hurts to miss at least four games, and the Super Bowl MVP will be sidelined for the remainder of the season.
summary: Quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after the Philadelphia Eagles revealed he had a blood clot in his calf. He had been ruled out on Thursday and was originally injured when a cleat struck his calf during the October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Daniel Dubois stops Fabio Wardley in second round to retain WBO heavyweight title
content:
Daniel Dubois retained his WBO heavyweight title on Saturday night with a second‑round stoppage of Fabio Wardley, underscoring his status as Britain’s leading heavyweight. The bout ended after 2 minutes and 21 seconds of the second round when the referee intervened as Wardley’s corner, led by trainer Ben Davison, threw in the towel.

The fight marked the second victory for Dubois over Wardley in five months, following their May encounter that was described as a “fight of the year contender.” Dubois opened the contest aggressively, dropping Wardley heavily just 17 seconds into the first round with a left cross followed by a crushing right hand.

Davison had been prepared to surrender at the close of the opening round, but the bell rang before he could do so. The referee’s stoppage came as the white towel was waved over the ropes, ending a one‑sided contest that left Wardley unable to recover from Dubois’s onslaught.
summary: Daniel Dubois stopped Fabio Wardley by referee intervention at 2:21 of the second round, retaining his WBO heavyweight title. Wardley’s corner threw in the towel after he was knocked down early in the round by a left cross and a right hand.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Air Force officer dies after falling from Alamodome rafters before UTSA-Navy game
content:
An Air Force officer died after falling from the rafters of the Alamodome during a pre‑game display for the University of Texas at San Antonio’s home football game against Navy on Saturday. The officer, whose name was not released, was participating in UTSA’s “Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans” night when he slipped while rappelling down from the stadium’s overhead structure.

He landed on the field and received immediate treatment before being placed on a stretcher and taken to a local hospital. He later succumbed to his injuries. Nellis Air Force Base identified the officer as a member of the 6th Combat Training Squadron, a unit that trains military personnel to rappel from helicopters. The incident occurred before the game began, prompting an abrupt end to the ceremonial display.
summary: Officer fell from rafters during pregame display Man treated on field before being taken to hospital An Air Force officer has died after he fell from the rafters of the Alamodome before the University of Texas at San Antonio’s home game against Navy on Saturday. The officer, who has not been named, was taking part in an event to celebrate UTSA’s Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans night.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wigan remain bottom of League One despite 1-0 win over Reading
content:
Wigan Athletic remain at the foot of League One even after a 1‑0 victory over Reading on Saturday, underscoring the gap between their current struggles and the club’s historic high point. The win did little to lift the Latics from the bottom of the third tier, a stark contrast to the euphoria of the 2013 FA Cup final when they famously defeated Manchester City.

Gary Caldwell, who captained the side in that triumph, is now manager and faces the task of turning the season around. Caldwell returned for a second spell after a stint at Exeter, a move seen as risky given the limited resources provided by owner Mike Danson, who is reportedly keen to sell the club. His earlier tenure saw Wigan promoted from the same division in 2015‑16, but the present campaign highlights the challenges of rebuilding under a shoestring budget.
summary: Wigan Athletic are bottom of League One even after a 1-0 victory over Reading on Saturday. Manager Gary Caldwell, the 2013 club captain, returned for a second stint while working under a shoestring budget imposed by owner Mike Danson, who is keen to sell.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig says he never enjoys games ahead of Liverpool match
content:
Villarreal owner Fernando Roig, Europe’s longest‑serving club president, admitted that he still does not enjoy watching his team play, even ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League tie at Anfield.  Roig, now in his 30th year at the helm and having overseen more than 1,000 matches, said the anxiety of the occasion “makes me suffer a lot.”

He recalled his first experience as president, when he watched Villarreal in the second division on a Sunday night at a small, half‑empty white‑washed ground and saw the side lose 3‑0 to Badajoz.  “I never enjoy it much,” he said, adding that the feeling has not changed despite the club’s progress to Europe’s elite stage.

Roig emphasized that the upcoming game is a symbol of how far the club has come, yet he remains “worried, very anxious” rather than simply nervous about the challenge at Liverpool.
summary: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig, Europe’s longest‑serving club president, says he never enjoys watching his team play. He said he feels anxious ahead of the Champions League match at Anfield against Liverpool, recalling his first game as president was a 3‑0 loss to Badajoz in the second division.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Three Premier League clubs struggling domestically meet in lesser European competition
content:
Four Premier League clubs are set to meet in the lesser continental competitions on Sunday, with three of the sides also battling domestic struggles. The fixtures take place in Leiria, Portugal, where a sunny day with temperatures in the high‑20s Celsius has created a convivial atmosphere for supporters and locals alike.

Fans have been able to secure tickets by emailing the president of Torreense, confirming the existence of the so‑called “Nuno‑tickets.” The venue, described as oversized for the match, allowed spectators to sit wherever they chose, and those who chose the hospitality seats at the back of the lower tier enjoyed free beer. A beer pump installed outside a patisserie on Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo saw patrons helping to stack empty barrels to keep the free flow of Sagres going.

Local residents expressed surprise at the influx but remained welcoming. The owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant recounted a town‑hall meeting that clarified the visiting fans were not hooligans, noting the club’s roots in the labour movement. She summed up the supporters as “noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.”
summary: Four Premier League clubs are playing each other on Sunday in the lesser continental competitions, with three of them also struggling in their domestic league. In Leiria, fans obtained tickets by emailing the president of Torreense, could sit anywhere in a large stadium, and enjoyed free beer provided by a local patisserie.
author: Guardian Sport

title: New Zealand Silver Ferns beat Australia 56-50 to open Constellation Cup
content:
The Silver Ferns opened the Constellation Cup with a 56‑50 victory over the world No. 1 Australian Diamonds at Auckland’s Spark Arena on Sunday, a result the title described as a “brave new world” for netball. Grace Nweke starred, converting 40 of 41 attempts as New Zealand signalled its intent to reshape the sport’s hierarchy.

New Zealand, the reigning Commonwealth Games gold medallists, continued the form they displayed in Glasgow, securing the series‑opening win. The Australian side missed the experienced duo of Jo Weston, who was managed, and Kate Moloney, who was sidelined with a finger injury.

The loss followed Australia’s shock semi‑final defeat to Jamaica, which left the Diamonds out of a gold‑medal match for the first time since netball entered the Games programme in 1998.
summary: The New Zealand Silver Ferns defeated the Australian Diamonds 56-50 at Spark Arena to open the Constellation Cup series. Australia were missing Jo Weston and Kate Moloney and had recently lost a Commonwealth Games semi‑final to Jamaica.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Emma Finucane takes bronze in women's keirin at UCI World Track Championships
content:
Great Britain's Emma Finucane took bronze in the women's keirin on the final day of the UCI World Track Championships in China after being beaten on the line.  

Finucane summed up the result as “It’s so close,” acknowledging the narrow margin.
summary: Great Britain's Emma Finucane was beaten on the line in the women's keirin. She settled for the bronze medal on the final day of the UCI World Track Championships in China.

title: Lara Gillespie wins second straight world title in points race at UCI Track Championships
content:
Lara Gillespie secured gold for Ireland, becoming world champion for a second consecutive season after dominating the points race on the final day of the UCI World Track Championships in China.  

The dramatic victory prompted the exclamation “What a finish!” as she clinched the title.
summary: Lara Gillespie of Ireland became world champion for a second consecutive season. She secured the title by dominating the points race on the final day of the UCI World Track Championships in China.
author: BBC Sport

title: Pedro Neto scores twice as Chelsea beat Everton 2-0
content:
Pedro Neto scored twice as Chelsea secured a 2-0 victory over Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.  

The win was largely eclipsed by a nasty head injury suffered by Everton goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez during the match.
summary: Pedro Neto scored twice for Chelsea as they defeated Everton 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. The game was overshadowed by a nasty head injury to Emiliano Martinez.
author: BBC Sport

title: Rep. Scott Perry trails Democratic challenger Janelle Stelson by three points in PA poll
content:
A new Susquehanna Polling and Research survey released Saturday shows incumbent Republican Rep. Scott Perry trailing Democratic challenger former news anchor Janelle Stelson in Pennsylvania's key battleground district.  

The poll reports Perry at 46 percent and Stelson at 49 percent, a three‑point gap that falls within the margin of error.
summary: A new Susquehanna Polling and Research survey of a Pennsylvania battleground district shows incumbent Rep. Scott Perry (R) trailing his Democratic opponent. The poll lists Perry at 46 % and former news anchor Janelle Stelson (D) at 49 %, a three‑point lead within the margin of error.

title: Trump issues executive order halting Russia sanctions, sparking bipartisan backlash
content: The Sunday preview highlighted an escalating feud between President Trump and President Zelensky and noted a wave of controversies confronting the White House ahead of the midterm elections. On Friday evening Trump issued an executive order that halted the rollout of new penalties on Russia set to take effect under a sweeping legislative package he signed last month, prompting bipartisan backlash over the administration’s recent easing of Russian sanctions.
summary: President Trump issued an executive order on Friday evening that stopped the implementation of new penalties on Russia set to take effect under a legislative package he signed into law last month. The order provoked bipartisan backlash and comes as the Trump‑Zelensky feud escalates and other controversies hit the White House before the midterms.

title: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemns attack on Washington Post photojournalist
content: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee denounced a “vicious” and “cowardly” assault on a Washington Post photojournalist in the West Bank, urging a full investigation. In a statement posted to X, Huckabee said the attack involved a group of Israeli settlers targeting Palestinians and the journalist.

content:

The waived measures originated from the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a bill Graham previously championed.

title: CDC deploys disease expert to Pennsylvania for measles outbreak response
content:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is dispatching a disease expert to Pennsylvania as the state confronts an ongoing measles outbreak.  

A CDC spokesperson told NBC News the agency will keep working closely with Pennsylvania health officials, offering the expertise and support needed to respond to the outbreak and protect public health.
summary: The CDC is sending a disease expert to assist with the response to the ongoing measles outbreak in Pennsylvania. A CDC spokesperson said the agency will continue working closely with Pennsylvania health officials to provide expertise and support to protect public health.

title: New federal rule makes flight compensation harder
content: A new federal rule is set to take effect, meaning passengers whose flights are delayed or canceled may find it harder to obtain compensation. The change applies to all airline travelers affected by cancellations or delays, altering the process for receiving monetary relief.
summary: A new federal rule is set to take effect. It could make it harder to obtain compensation for delayed or canceled flights.

title: Call for research, safeguards and guidance to protect children from AI
content: The article asserts that children will inevitably grow up with artificial intelligence and calls for the development of research, safeguards and scientific guidance to understand AI’s effects on them, urging action while the opportunity still exists to shape future outcomes.
summary: The piece says children will grow up with artificial intelligence. It urges building research, safeguards and scientific guidance to understand AI’s impact on children while there is still an opportunity to shape the future.

title: President Zelensky meets UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham at Downing Street
content: Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Volodymyr Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday. The Ukrainian leader’s visit comes as he looks to shore up his European allies five years into Russia’s war on Ukraine.
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday. Zelensky is looking to shore up his European allies five years into Russia's war on Ukraine.

title: Reform UK says no room for racism after ITV airs councillors' racist remarks
content: Reform UK faces criticism after ITV News aired undercover footage recorded over a year that captured some of its councillors and candidates using racist, violent and sexist language. The party responded that there is no room for racism within Reform UK.
summary: Reform UK said there is no room for racism in its party. The comment followed ITV News broadcasting undercover footage, collected over a year, of some Reform UK councillors and candidates using racist, violent and sexist language.

title: Iguazu Falls reaches record flow ten times normal, prompting temporary closure
content:
Iguazu Falls, a UNESCO World Heritage site in South America, has recorded a water flow ten times its normal rate after heavy rains across the river basin. El Niño weather patterns are said to have driven the surge, with the usual flow of 1.5 million litres per second rising to 15 million litres per second, according to the local government.

In response to the El Niño‑fuelled increase in water levels, Argentina has temporarily closed Iguazu Falls. The unprecedented flow underscores the impact of the current weather conditions on the iconic waterfall.
summary: Iguazu Falls, a UNESCO world heritage site, recorded a water flow of 15 million litres per second—about ten times its normal 1.5 million litres per second—after heavy rains and El Niño conditions. Argentina temporarily closed the falls due to the surge in water levels.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Insider claims insurers cut loss forecasts to lower prices despite rising climate risk
content:
An anonymous modeller employed by a major insurer has disclosed that the industry is increasingly under‑reporting the financial impact of natural‑disaster losses. The whistle‑blower, who assesses risk for properties ranging from family homes to multibillion‑dollar commercial centres, says insurers are taking on more risk than they can sustain and that “if – or when – a major disaster hits, the catastrophe will have far‑reaching consequences” for the global financial system.

According to the account, pressure is being placed on the modeller to cut loss forecasts so that insurance premiums appear more affordable and the firm can win business against lower‑priced rivals. While the modeller acknowledges that some scrutiny of models is justified, they claim that “too often, it is not being done to produce more accurate models, but to artificially lower prices,” a practice they say is spreading across the sector.

The piece was originally published by the Bureau of Investigative Journalism as part of its Secret Source series, which features industry whistle‑blowers.
summary: An anonymous insurance modeller says insurers are taking on more risk than they should and are being pressured to cut loss forecasts for natural disasters. He alleges the lowered forecasts are often used to artificially reduce prices and win business, and the piece was first published in the Bureau of Investigative Journalism’s Secret Source series.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Coalition says emissions from Australian fossil fuels burned abroad should be ignored
content:
The Coalition has suggested that emissions from Australian fossil fuels burned overseas should be ignored, arguing that accounting for them is “madness.” The position, highlighted in a Temperature Check commentary, notes that while the emissions occur abroad, scientists can now quantify the global harm they cause. The piece points out that concern over this issue includes a majority of high‑court judges and the International Court of Justice.

Climate and environment editor Adam Morton, who writes the Clear Air column, urges readers to sign up for his free newsletter for further analysis.
summary: The Coalition proposes treating emissions from Australian fossil fuels burned overseas as non‑existent. Those emissions have drawn concern from a majority of high court judges and the International Court of Justice.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Reform UK councillor scraps King's Lynn climate emergency declaration after heated vote
content:
The debate over climate‑emergency declarations resurfaced in King’s Lynn and West Norfolk after the council, which had first declared a climate emergency in 2021 while under Conservative control, changed hands to independents and a Reform UK councillor. Reform UK councillor Austen Moore moved to overturn the declaration; the meeting was postponed because extreme heat made the council chamber unusable, and the motion was subsequently rescheduled and defeated by a vote of 33 to seven.

A liveblog by a local scientist and Extinction Rebellion member recorded the proceedings, adding maps that showed most of the county, including King’s Lynn, already lies below the annual flood level. The article notes that similar debates have occurred in other Reform‑led councils, where Reform’s arguments have prevailed. In Kent, councillor Linden Kemkaran argued that climate change is acceptable because the world was warmer in Roman times and that carbon dioxide is a trace gas essential for life, suggesting that cutting emissions would be dangerous.

The piece concludes by promoting the Guardian’s Climate Forum 2026, scheduled for 20 October, featuring Zoe Williams alongside a panel that includes professor Andrew Haines, MP Katie White, Asad Rehman, Shruti Suresh, Gareth Thomas and Amy Fairman. The forum is billed as a hopeful, solutions‑focused evening.
summary: The King's Lynn and West Norfolk council, now controlled by independents and Reform UK councillor Austen Moore, voted 33‑to‑7 to scrap its 2021 climate‑emergency declaration. The motion was delayed because extreme heat forced the council chamber to close, and the vote took place the following week.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Protected sand tiger sharks sold abroad via Delaware Bay loophole
content:
A loophole in U.S. fisheries regulations is allowing private companies to capture protected sand‑tiger sharks and sell them to overseas aquariums, critics say, even as the species benefits from conservation gains in Delaware Bay. While state anglers are barred from taking the endangered fish, the exemption permits commercial firms to harvest the sharks for export, prompting concerns that the Bay’s recent recovery is being monetised.

At about 12:45 p.m., researchers from the University of Delaware witnessed the capture of a sand‑tiger shark on a 300‑metre line in the bay’s murky green waters. The 225‑centimetre, 90‑centimetre‑girth shark was hauled aboard a small boat, measured, sexed and sampled for blood and muscle. A tag was then secured beneath its dorsal fin through its thick, sand‑papery skin, enabling future monitoring of the species despite its removal from the wild.
summary: A loophole permits private firms to catch protected sand tiger sharks in Delaware Bay for export to foreign aquariums, despite bans on anglers taking the endangered species. University of Delaware researchers recently captured, measured, sampled and tagged a 225 cm sand tiger shark in the bay.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Gabon battles US drug firms to protect iboga, a sacred plant eyed for addiction treatment
content:
Gabon is fighting US drug companies to safeguard iboga, a sacred plant that some compare to ayahuasca.  

The bitter root bark, known as iboga, is central to several Gabonese ritual traditions and is believed to have huge potential for treating addiction and some mental illnesses. In a dark temple with a sandy floor edged with candles, participants sit shoulder to shoulder beneath palm fronds and swallow the bark throughout the night.  

Iboga comes from Tabernanthe iboga, a slow‑growing central African rainforest shrub whose root bark has long been used in Gabonese rituals.
summary: Gabon is fighting to protect the iboga root, a sacred plant used in several Gabonese ritual traditions, from US drug companies. The plant’s bark is believed to have huge potential for treating addiction and some mental illnesses.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Miami’s Spice N Curry owner says $370K pandemic loan became a disaster
content:
The Covid‑19 pandemic left many restaurants reeling, and the federal disaster loans intended to help are now proving a new burden, as illustrated by Miami’s Spice N Curry. Owner Jai Mazumdar, who has run the vegetarian‑focused café and grocery near Florida International University for almost two decades, secured a $370,000 Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) in early 2021. The loan offered a 3.75 % interest rate and a 30‑month deferment, with repayment spread over 30 years, giving Mazumdar confidence that the business could bounce back and meet its obligations.

However, the expected recovery never materialized. With sales still far below pre‑pandemic levels, Mazumdar now faces a debt that has become a “disaster of its own,” underscoring how the relief program intended to sustain eateries is instead adding long‑term financial strain.
summary: Jai Mazumdar, owner of Spice N Curry near Florida International University, took a $370,000 Economic Injury Disaster Loan in early 2021. The restaurant’s post‑pandemic recovery fell short, turning the low‑interest loan into a financial burden.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Salk Institute maps exercise's molecular effects across mouse organs, cells, sexes
content: Salk Institute researchers are creating a scientific reference for bodily health by mapping how exercise reshapes the body at the molecular level. Their latest effort examines exercise‑induced responses across multiple organs, cell types, sexes and circadian phases in mice, aiming to define what a healthy body looks like before studying disease.
summary: Salk Institute researchers are creating a scientific reference for what makes a body healthy. Their latest study maps how exercise reshapes the body at the molecular level, examining responses across organs, cell types, sexes and circadian phases in mice.

title: Body data may give 24‑hour warning for post‑concussion headaches
content: Researchers have found that the headaches and fatigue many concussion sufferers experience follow a consistent pattern that could be used to warn patients a full day before the symptoms set in. The observation suggests that monitoring body data may provide a 24‑hour advance alert for these post‑concussion effects.
summary: Some people who suffer a concussion experience headaches and fatigue afterward. The symptoms follow a consistent pattern that could be used to warn the patient a full day before they set in.

title: Lab-designed synthetic peptide reduces amyloid beta in mice
content: A research team led by the Molecular and Cellular Neurobiotechnology group at the Institute for Bioengineering of Catalonia (IBEC) has identified a synthetic peptide that lowers the production of amyloid beta (Aβ), the protein linked to Alzheimer’s disease, in mice. The work was carried out in collaboration with Míriam Royo’s laboratory at the Institute for Advanced Chemistry of Catalonia (IQAC‑CSIC), the University of Barcelona and the Institute for Research in Biomedicine (IRB Barcelona). The discovery marks a laboratory‑designed molecule capable of reducing amyloid beta levels in an animal model.
